title: Retargeting Video Ad Template | AIVideosUGC
description: Bring viewed products back with a retargeting video from one photo. Show a clear detail, add a confirmed offer after download, and post where they shop.
h1: Retargeting Video Ad for Shoppers Who Already Looked
lead: Make a new clip for a product people already saw, then add the current offer after download.
steps_h2: Make a Remarketing Video Ad in 3 Steps
steps_lead: The clip is a new video. It does not know who viewed the product or left a cart.

steps.d: Upload one photo that shows the product and the detail worth a second look. Keep that detail in frame.
Describe one closer look, then pick a size and a length from 6 to 30 seconds. Leave cart status out of the scene.
Download the clip and add the current offer in your editor. Choose the audience in your ad platform.

faq.q: What is a retargeting video ad here?
faq.a: A new product clip for people who already saw an item. A cart reminder video can use this creative, but the file has no viewer list. You choose the audience, exclusions and frequency in your ad platform.

faq.q: Does AIVideosUGC know who viewed a product or left a cart?
faq.a: No. The clip does not receive browsing or cart data. You choose the audience in your ad platform, and the scene only shows the product.

faq.q: How do I make the second look?
faq.a: Upload a photo that shows the detail worth revisiting, describe that one closer look, pick a size and length, then download.
Electronics and fashion shops running remarketing on Facebook or Instagram, and anyone who needs a fresh creative rather than a repeat of the first ad.
One detail the first view may have missed: a lid, a zipper, a finish or a daily-use moment. Keep the product as the subject.

faq.q: Which size and length should I pick?
faq.a: 1:1 for a feed and 9:16 for Reels are the usual pair, plus 16:9, 4:3 or 3:4. Lengths are 6, 10, 15 or 30 seconds.

faq.q: Can I put the current offer on the video here?
faq.a: Add the confirmed price, date or link after download. If the offer changes, edit that text on the file you already have.

faq.q: Can I test more than one second look?
faq.a: Yes. Make another scene from the same photo and compare the files in your ad platform. You do not need a new shoot for each angle.
24 credits for 6 seconds, 40 for 10, 60 for 15 and 120 for 30. You see the cost first. A failed job returns its credits. Plans start at $24.50 a month.
As creative in a remarketing campaign, a feed post or a Reels ad. The download has no watermark. Any person on screen is an AI performer, not a past buyer.

steps.sourceAlt: Dark navy over-ear headphones with padded ear cups on a pale background.
steps.sourceHint: Keep the complete headband and both ear cups in clear focus.
steps.prompt: An adult wearing the over-ear headphones walks along a bright station platform and turns toward an arriving train, with both ear cups visible.

picker.title: Choose a Scene for a Remarketing Video Ad
picker.lead: Open a product scene and show one detail worth a second look. You choose who sees it in your ad platform.

cards.label: ASMR Unboxing: Makeup Tools
cards.prompt: A seller can open with a close unboxing that lifts your makeup tools from tissue paper and puts the brush set in clear view.

cards.label: Cinematic Watch Detail
cards.prompt: A cinematic close-up can hold your watch in warm light while the camera glides across its face and strap.

cards.label: Bedroom Try-On: Knitwear
cards.prompt: Show your knitwear in a bedroom try-on as the creator turns in the mirror so the fit and sleeves stay visible.

cards.label: Street Style: Linen Set
cards.prompt: Take your linen set outdoors for a street-style walk that shows the fabric, movement and full silhouette.

cards.label: Lifestyle App Recommendation
cards.prompt: A creator can recommend your app from a real kitchen table while tapping through a clean, abstract interface on a phone.

cards.label: Streamer Reaction: App
cards.prompt: Use a streamer-style reaction to show the moment your app surprises a viewer, with the device screen kept clear and easy to follow.

cards.label: Routine Demo: Cream
cards.prompt: Film a quick morning routine where a creator opens your cream jar and applies it at a bright vanity.

cards.label: Bathroom Review: Moisturizer
cards.prompt: Let a creator give a direct bathroom review while holding your moisturizer beside his face and turning the jar toward the camera.

cards.label: GRWM Unboxing: Knitwear
cards.prompt: Build a get-ready moment around opening your knit sweater parcel and holding the full garment up before styling it.

cards.label: Mirror Selfie: Denim
cards.prompt: A mirror selfie can show your denim overshirt from collar to hem as the creator checks the fit before heading out.

cards.label: 360 Showcase: Linen Shirt
cards.prompt: Rotate your linen shirt through a clean 360 showcase so shoppers can inspect the collar, seams and full shape.

cards.label: Street Interview: Fitness Gear

cards.label: Tutor Demo: Study Tool
cards.prompt: A teacher can demonstrate your study tool at a classroom desk with a simple lesson that keeps the product in use.

cards.label: Talking Head: Skin Lesson
cards.prompt: Use a clear talking-head lesson to explain how your moisturizer fits a simple daily routine, with the jar held beside the speaker.

cards.label: POV Discovery: Court Gear
cards.prompt: Open from an athlete's point of view as your court gear is picked up and shown where the next play starts.

cards.label: Hook: Home App Walkthrough

cards.label: Finance Hook: Phone Demo
cards.prompt: Use a direct phone demo to introduce your finance app and show the key navigation without exposing private figures.

cards.label: Realtor Walkthrough: Home
